title: CWP/5782/2025 of M/S MATHRA DASS AHUJA AND SONS Vs STATE OF HARYANA AND OTHERS
petitioner: M/S Mathra Dass Ahuja And Sons
text:
2025 PHHC 06803 IN THE HIGH COURT OF PUNJAB AND HARYANA AT CHANDIGARH 112 CWP No.5782 of 2025 DATE OF DECISION : 20" May, 2025 M/s. Mathra Dass Ahuja & Sons New Delhi .... Petitioner Versus State of Haryana & others .... Respondents 112-A CWP No.5786 of 2024 M/s. Mathra Dass Ahuja & Sons New Delhi .... Petitioner Versus State of Haryana & others .... Respondents CORAM : HON’BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP TIWARI 2k ok ok ok Present: Ms. Ojaswini Gagneja, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. Bhupender Singh, DAG, Haryana with Mr. Anil Kumar Dahiya, Engineer-in-Chief, PWD B & R, Haryana. ook ok ok KULDEEP TIWARI, J. (Oral)

1. Since a common issue involves in both the petitions, therefore, both being amenable for common decision, same are taken up together.

2. Through the instant writ petition(s) filed under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India, challenge is thrown to the order dated 08.08.2024 (Annexure P-13), passed by respondent No.4, to the extent that the authority concerned, will make the payments to the petitioner only upon the allotment of funds, for which approval has not been sanctioned by respondent No.1. RAJ KUMAR I /judgment CWP No.5782 of 2025 & CWP No.5786 of 2025 2025 PHHC 068039 § 3. At the time of issuance of notice of motion this court has passed the hereinafter extracted order: RAJ KUMAR I /judgment “While referring to the reply to the legal notice served by the petitioner, learned counsel for the petitioner inter alia submits that despite specific admission on the part of the respondents concerned, the respondents are not releasing the funds, only on the premise, that the matter is under consideration, before the higher authorities concerned, and the due amount will be paid, as soon as the funds for the same seems to be allowed by the authorities concerned. Learned counsel further submits that though there is an arbitration clause, but since there is no dispute with regard to the amount due, as emerges from the speaking order (Annexure P-13), therefore, there is no reason for the petitioner to invoke the dispute redressal clause. Notice of motion. Mr. Bhupender Singh, DAG, Haryana, has caused appearance, waives service and accepts notice on behalf of all the respondents. He seeks some time to file response to the instant petition. List this matter on 29.04.2025. On the next date of hearing, the respondents shall inform this Court, with regard to the time required by the higher authorities concerned, to take a final decision, in respect to the claim of the petitioner.” CWP No.5782 of 2025 & CWP No.5786 of 2025 2025 PHHC 068039 fe

4. Learned State counsel, on instructions imparted from Mr. Anil Kumar Dahiya, Engineer-in-Chief, PWD B & R, Haryana, submits that the sanction has been duly accorded for disbursal of the amount in question to the petitioner(s)-firm, and also a communication in this regard bearing Memo No.67742 dated 19.05.2025, has also been communicated to the petitioner(s). He further submits that a token number in this regard has been generated, and within next seven working days the amount will be transferred in the account of the petitioner(s)- firm.

5. In view of the specific stand taken by the learned counsel for the State, no further direction is required to be issued in the instant matter(s). Consequently, the instant petitions are ordered to be closed. However, in case the petitioner(s) still fetches any grievance with regard to the interest part, then the petitioner(s) will be at liberty to approach the apt authority/forum by moving an apt motion for redressal of its grievances.

6. In view of the above, both the petitions are disposed of accordingly, with liberty as aforesaid. 20" May, 2025 ( KULDEEP TIWARI ) ‘raj’ JUDGE I /judgment
